title: Grainline customer harvest + feature funnel brief
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a compact harvest from the last 6 weeks of frontline threads with customers using Hosted API and Dedicated. Aim: extract vignettes that point to low-friction fixes, mid-effort features, and longer-term platform asks we should feed into the product funnel. Not exhaustive — intended to seed a micro-sprint of 2-week probes.

How this doc was made:
- Sources: 12 support threads, 3 post-call notes with mid-market customers, internal SRE runbook comments, and one field interview (Aug 2027).
- Tagging heuristic: latency-foreground, output-quality, deployment friction, cost-related.
- Quick validation: prioritized by frequency and estimated user impact; numbers are qualitative.

Topline signals (short):
- Repeated ask: clearer guidance and quick defaults for KV cache tuning when customers enable long-chat sessions (esp > 8k tokens).
- Multiple customers hit a throughput wall with small-batch streaming + prefix-caching — results: token latency spikes under load.
- Several customers want an automated model-variant fallback that preserves structure for tool-calls (not just text).
- Cost sensitivity: teams want a per-route suggestion for batched vs streaming throughput to minimize per-token cost without blowing latency SLOs.

Representative vignettes (anonymized):
1) "Topline marketplace" (SaaS, 120M prompts/mo): seeing token tail-latency after ~90s of sustained chat; ops team suspects cache eviction churn is interacting with small batch sizes. Current workaround: reduce sequence length but hurts UX.
2) "Reg-comms" (enterprise legal): worried about model fallback behavior — when their primary model is down, fallback returned a different function schema causing downstream failures in their ingestion pipeline. They ask for schema-preserving fallbacks.
3) "CX automation" (mid-market): would trade small accuracy for 35% cost reduction on embeddings pipeline. Wants a recommended quantization and batching profile per workload.

Candidate quick patches (low effort, high impact):
A) KV-cache diagnostics endpoint (S) — expose a simple API that returns current cache hit-rate estimates and recent eviction reasons per customer. Why: customers can confirm whether their tail-latency is cache-related before involving SRE. Suggested owner: infra-telemetry. Jira: JIRA-CUST-3197.
Estimated effort: small. Metrics to watch: cache_hit_rate, eviction_count, median_token_latency.

B) Rolling default for streaming+small-batch mode (S) — tweak runtime default batching when streaming with prefix-caching to hold a tiny adaptive window rather than immediate flush. Why: empirically reduces token tail latency for many small interactive sessions. Suggested owner: serving-runtime.
Estimated effort: small-medium (runtime change + limited canary).

C) Fallback schema guard (M) — a lightweight wrapper that verifies function/schema compatibility before returning fallback output; if incompatible, trigger a structured error + optional simple text fallback. Why: prevents pipeline breakage for tool-calling customers. Suggested owner: console-and-rollouts + serving-runtime.
Estimated effort: medium. Acceptance: end-to-end test covering tool schemas.

Mid-effort features (should enter product funnel):
1) Per-route cost-performance advisor (M) — in Console, present a small recommendation card: "Use batching profile X for @route to save ~Y% cost with <Zms latency impact". Backed by historical traces. Integrates with Optimize's recommendations.
Rationale: repeated asks from PLG customers and platform teams; reduces back-and-forth with solutions engineers.

2) Model-variant graceful-fallback orchestration (M-L) — allow customers to define "compatibility rules" for fallback variants (e.g., preserve: function-calling schema, embedding-dim). Add test harness to simulate capacity failures and validate fallbacks.
Customer value: reduces production surprises; supports Dedicated customers wanting predictable behavior.

3) Embedded-probe for quantization impact (M) — a lightweight lab that runs a few representative queries against float32 vs quantized variants and reports per-query deltas (coherence, hallucination risk indicators).
Why: customers asking to trade quality for cost in a controlled way.

Prioritization notes (why these first):
- Quick patches A/B have low engineering risk and address root causes in multiple vignettes (latency + schema breakage).
- Mid-effort features reduce customer support overhead and are potential revenue enablers for Dedicated.

Open questions to resolve before a patch sprint:
- Ownership: who owns the public-facing KV cache diagnostics UI (console vs infra telemetry)?
- Data retention for per-route advisor: what's a reasonable retention window (30d?) to give stable suggestions without leaking sensitive payloads?
- Can we automatically detect "function schema incompatibility" for arbitrary user-defined tools or do we require a customer-provided compatibility manifest?

Quick experiment ideas (2-week probes):
- Probe 1: Enable KV-cache diagnostics for 5 pilot customers and observe whether they self-resolve latency tickets. Success: fewer support escalations and faster triage time.
- Probe 2: Launch an opt-in runtime canary where streaming with prefix-caching uses a 10–50ms adaptive batching window. Monitor tail token latency and error rates.
- Probe 3: Offer a "schema-guarded fallback" toggle to 3 enterprise customers and collect false-positive/negative rates for schema-preserving behavior.

Acceptance criteria for the micro-sprint:
- KV diagnostics endpoint returns clear metrics and is documented in runbook within 5 business days of rollout.
- Streaming-batching canary reduces 95th token-latency by at least 20% for pilot traffic without increasing error-rate > 0.5%.
- Schema-guarded fallback pilot shows <2% legitimate-blocks (cases where guard prevented safe fallback).

Operational considerations and risks:
- Exposing cache internals increases support noise if not properly documented — include an "interpreting dashboard" doc.
- Any adaptive batching change requires careful kernel path testing (some models are sensitive to micro-batching changes). Coordinate with release-engineering.
- Fallback guard could delay failover; must ensure timeouts are conservative.

Suggested next steps (owner assignments):
- Asha P. (CS) to align pilot customer list and co-ordinate outreach (this doc owner).
- Jonah R. (Serving-runtime) to scope streaming-batching canary and propose a minimal config.
- Priya S. (Infra-telemetry) to prototype KV diagnostics API and a console stub.
- Schedule: 1 week scoping, 2-week pilot, 1-week evaluation -> decision to roadmap.

Appendix: quick customer asks snapshot (single lines)
- "We need a quick toggle to force no-fallback — safer for legal workflows."
- "Can you recommend a quantization profile for low-cost embeddings?"
- "Why did my tool call return different fields after the model switched?"

Links & refs:
- JIRA-CUST-3197: customer report and thread (detailed error logs).
- CONFLUENCE-5241: previous KV cache notes (internal).
- Git PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/182 (telemetry schema change).

Notes to self: keep language simple in customer comms. For pilots, prepare a short script for onboarding and an FAQ.
